answer: In a harbor marketplace, AI agents booking a voyage for marble cargo must each lock a $1,000 bond for 30 days before bidding, and each bonded identity may hold only one active contract. Creating 1,000 fake identities therefore requires $1 million in locked capital, not merely new keys. The delay prevents an attacker from recycling one bond across aliases during a bidding round, making a swarm costly even when its bonds are eventually returned.
